fields.v: Conceptual — essay arguing that reproducible research practices are context engineering for AI coding agents; catalog mapping artefacts to context categories, plus an 'invocation layer' of commands/skills

No named SDD approach. Author's catalog of 'agent-facing artifacts' (reproducible-research practices reframed as context engineering) plus an 'invocation layer' of slash commands and skills that write to project files. Version: N/A

Agent instruction file AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (always-on semantic memory; six areas: commands, testing, structure, code style, git workflow, boundaries always/ask first/never); test suite of characterization tests (executable semantic memory, 'a specification of expected behavior'); commit history with Conventional Commits (episodic memory); repository structure (pre-processed context); decision record DECISIONS.md in ADR format (static context)
Not stated as a flow; artefacts drafted by the agent on request (e.g. /commit, decision-record skill, changelog skill) and verified by the researcher
Researcher as 'owner and verifier' of every agent-drafted artefact: confirms test intent, edits commit messages, supplies tacit knowledge and decision reasoning
Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'context engineering at the timescale of a codebase'; tests as executable specification)
Existing research code bases (research software maintenance); not run
Researchers and graduate students who are 'not trained or paid to be software engineers'
None measured (qualitative claim that per-session friction collapses)
N/A (no comparison; argument draws on a cited GitHub analysis of 2,500 agent instruction files and an RSE vision statement)
N/A. Qualitative: four of the six areas of effective agent instruction files (commands, testing, structure, git workflow) match reproducibility practices cleanly; code style and boundaries partly

Artefacts do not prevent researchers accepting agent output without understanding (skill erosion); generation stays non-deterministic; productivity is not a fix for research incentives; untouched: training-data provenance and attribution, unequal access to frontier tools, institutional disinvestment in people

No empirical data; no replication package (N/A). No pre-registration. Main evidence is a cited industry analysis of 2,500 instruction files [4] and the Edinburgh RSE workshop vision statement [10]. Artefact table (p. 3) jumbled in text extraction; rebuilt from the prose. Language: N/A
Yes (1): thesis stated in abstract and introduction
